testCases.name: returns none for missing keys
testCases.description: Reading an absent key is a cache miss.
testCases.feedback: Return None without changing recency when the key is absent.

testCases.name: updating a key replaces its ttl
testCases.description: A live update starts a fresh TTL from the update time.
testCases.feedback: Replace both value and expires_at when updating a live key.

testCases.name: updating without a ttl removes the previous deadline
testCases.description: A live update with ttl=None changes an expiring entry into a non-expiring entry.
testCases.feedback: Replace expires_at with None when an existing key is updated without a TTL.

testCases.name: negative capacity stores no entries
testCases.description: A non-positive capacity can't retain an entry or evict from an empty cache.
testCases.feedback: Clamp negative capacity to zero before applying the eviction loop.

testCases.name: capacity one evicts the previous key
testCases.description: In a one-entry cache, inserting a second live key removes the first.
testCases.feedback: Evict the least-recent live entry before storing beyond capacity.

testCases.name: negative ttl replacement invalidates only its own key

clarifyingQuestions: Are expired entries removed lazily or by background cleanup?
Should metrics distinguish TTL eviction from capacity eviction?
followUps: Add thread safety with an RLock around map and recency order.
followUpGuide: For metrics, increment hits only after the expiry check succeeds. Expired entries should count as misses and optionally as TTL evictions.
For thread safety, wrap `get`, `put`, cleanup, and eviction in one `threading.RLock`. OrderedDict recency mutation is shared state.
For stale-while-revalidate, store both `expires_at` and `stale_until`. Return stale values inside the stale window while one background refresh owns the reload.
complexityAnalysis: - List scan approach: store entries in an array and move keys by scanning. Time: O(n) per get/set. Space: O(n).

- OrderedDict solution: expected hash lookup plus recency ordering. Time: O(1) expected per get or write that does not exceed capacity; O(n) for a capacity-reclaiming write that scans expired entries. Space: O(n), including the temporary snapshot used for safe cleanup iteration. n is the number of retained entries (at most capacity + 1 during a write).

- Expiry-heap follow-up: with h heap records, Time: O(log h) per expiring write or cleanup pop; a call removing k records costs O(k log h). Space: O(n + h). Lazy invalidation leaves stale records after updates, so h need not be bounded by cache capacity; add compaction or indexed deletion to keep space O(n).
solutionGuide: Use `collections.OrderedDict` to keep keys in recency order. Move a key to the end on every successful `get` and every `put`.

[`OrderedDict.move_to_end`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.html#collections.OrderedDict.move_to_end) changes order explicitly; `popitem(last=False)` removes the oldest entry. Ordinary insertion-ordered dictionaries do not move an existing key on assignment.
Store each value with `expires_at`. Before capacity eviction, scan and remove expired keys so stale entries don't evict live entries.
return expires_at is not None and self.now() >= expires_at
def put(self, key: str, value, ttl: float | None = None) -> None:
expires_at = None if ttl is None else self.now() + ttl
For a threaded follow-up, one lock must protect both the dictionary and order mutations. Recency is shared mutable state.
